subject: Postcall: AtlasSearch embeddings — dimensionality probe & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Turner <ari@atlassearch.com>, Samir Patel <samir@atlassearch.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-22T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Postcall: AtlasSearch embeddings — dimensionality probe & next steps

Thanks for the time today — quick recap and proposed next steps from our end.

Summary of call
- Goal: replace current semantic retrieval with a production embedding index for search & recommendations.
- Primary constraints: sub-200ms query P95, 50M doc index, and low drift risk across frequent content updates.
- Immediate ask from Atlas: a short pilot to validate model fit on their news+kb mix, with clear metrics for semantic search and drift.

Redwood recommendations (initial)
1) Candidate models: text-embed-redwood-compact-v1 (64d, 384d variants) and open-embedding-xl-128
2) Start with a 128-d configuration for balance of capacity and retrieval accuracy; we'll run a dimensionality probe as part of the pilot.
3) Benchmarks: semantic search MRR/Recall@10, pairwise cosine margin, index size per million docs, and upstream drift score (token distribution + centroid shift).

Deliverables we propose
- 1-week dimensionality probe: run on a 100k seed of Atlas docs to compare 64/128/384 dims (benchmarks + memory/latency tradeoffs).
- Prompt set and eval harness: we will share a 40-query prompt set and a small labeled relevance sample for QA-style queries.
- Quick demo: 30-min results walkthrough once probe completes.

Next steps (action items)
- Ari: confirm dataset export (S3 link or shared Drive) and preferred NDA scope (if any) — due Thu 3/24.
- Marissa/Karthik: provision probe, share prompt_set_atlas_v1.txt and benchmark script; deliver initial results within 5 business days.
- Vanessa: start procurement conversation for a trial Dedicated slot if probe looks promising.

Attachments: atlas_embed_benchmarks_v0.csv (sample rows), prompt_set_atlas_v1.txt (candidate queries)

Best,

Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear plan. A few quick answers and a follow-up question.

Data: we'll share an S3 export (s3://atlas-prod/exports/embed-probe-20280322) with text + doc metadata. We'll open a shared Drive folder with a labeled sample (50 positive/negative relevance judgments).

NDA/procurement: we'll use the standard Atlas mutual NDA (no special clauses). Procurement sign-off may be slow on Dedicated; for the probe we can run on Redwood hosted.

Prompt set: can you also share a smaller 20-query business-critical subset first? Our product team wants to validate against high-frequency user queries before the full 40.

One technical note: our content includes short headlines (~8-15 tokens) and long explainers (~700 tokens). Curious how you plan to handle variable sequence lengths for the probe.

—Ari

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Postcall: AtlasSearch embeddings — dimensionality probe & next steps

Great — thanks for the S3 path, Ari. We'll pick up the export and start the probe tomorrow morning.

Regarding the prompt set: attaching prompt_set_atlas_v1.txt (40 queries) and a smaller file prompt_set_atlas_quick_20.txt (first 20 queries for the product team's quick check). You'll see the queries split across short-head vs long-tail to reflect your content mix.

Sequence-length handling (quick approach)
- For the probe we'll run two passes: (A) full-text embeddings (truncate at 1024 tokens) and (B) headline-only embeddings to mirror short-query behavior. We'll compare retrieval metrics by query type.

Dimensionality + quality note: in prior pilots we observed a centroid collapse effect when using aggressively-low dimensions (64d) on mixed long/short corpora — recall dropped ~4-6% on long-form relevance for one client. That's why we recommend the 128-d baseline and explicitly include recall-by-length slices in the report. If we see a regression at 64d, mitigation paths are: (1) use hybrid indexing (title-only/long-doc separate indexes), (2) increase dimensionality, or (3) apply small sparse re-ranking model to catch edge cases.

Links and attachments
- Drive folder (shared): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AtlasEmbedEval
- Initial benchmark harness (readme in Drive) and sample output: https://eva.redwood.ai/results/DEAL-4821/embed-bench-v0
- Attached: atlas_embed_benchmarks_v0.csv (sample rows), prompt_set_atlas_v1.txt, prompt_set_atlas_quick_20.txt

We'll target an internal run by EOD Wed and a results deck for the 30-min walkthrough on Mon 3/28.

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa Cole
